goal: Use Continuity to move through the internet, connected systems, and other external surfaces without getting lost. External things remain external; Continuity records the relational trail of what was touched, why it was touched, what changed, what branch was taken, and where movement went next.
next_movement: Connect browser/search/social/news/video/forum/documentation/marketplace/job/map/public-data adapters to the generic traversal trace. Each adapter should emit bounded touch records instead of importing its source into Continuity.
walls: Do not redefine A/B as Continuity, traversal, the trace store, the portal, or the internet.
Do not put the internet inside Continuity.
External state stays external; Continuity preserves the trace of movement through it.
Do not create a new top-level architecture for every website, feed, content type, or provider.
Do not confuse browser navigation with relational movement; a touch must preserve why the source mattered to the current referent.
Do not turn every touch into a task, handoff, plan, reminder, or saved artifact.
Do not treat touching or reading a source as proof that its claims are true.
Do not erase source attribution when information crosses layers.
Do not let old trace ancestry override the current referent.
Do not make education, production, research, social interaction, news, or any other one surface the site focus.
Do not treat simulated traversal as real external evidence.

handoff.from: Continuity Portal → Human Areas over Connected Sources
handoff.reason: The portal areas remain valid, but external internet content should not be modeled as more internal source systems. Continuity is the layer used while moving through those external surfaces so the relational thread remains traceable.

human_areas.rule: Human areas are entrances for what a person is doing. They are not copies of internet platforms or content categories.

external_traversal.rule: External state stays external; Continuity preserves the trace of movement through it.
external_traversal.touch: A bounded record of an external locator, current referent, relation/reason, ancestry, and what changed.
external_traversal.trace: Reachable ancestry of touches that explains how the current referent moved.

checks: External surfaces are cataloged separately from human areas.
A generic append-only trace carrier records touches without copying external content.
Recording a touch does not create work or handoffs.
HTTP endpoints expose trace recording/listing/ancestry for future adapters.
